reviewedBy: Claude (Opus 5), session 57b768fe, reading the pasted bookmarklet capture with Jacob Kennedy
source: bookmarklet capture via the Woo Store API, 32 of 33 products
recommendation: DO NOT PUBLISH. `pending` stays true. Read the review.
review: THIS IS NOT A GAMING MERCHANT AND THE CATALOGUE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS. Every one of the 32 products is 12V lead-acid battery maintenance: trickle chargers and solar maintainers 'for RV Boat Marine Motorcycle Trailer Truck Tractor', plus seven solar panels sold specifically to power a deer feeder. Nothing here plugs into a desk, a handheld or a console. The room is called Power and the shelf would read as a farm supply store.

The registry is what made it look plausible. `room:'power'` was assigned from the brand name before anybody read the feed, and the Power room's own blurb is 'Chargers, cables, and the brick you keep losing'. A 30W solar panel on an adjustable rack is not that brick.

HELD AT pending: true. The reviewed file exists so nobody reads this catalogue a second time, not because it cleared. publishable() needs BOTH a reviewed file and a cleared flag, which is exactly the case this split was built for: understood, and understood to be wrong for the shelf.

The nearest thing to a crossover is the three 'Portable Foldable Solar Panel Charger Kit for Power Stations and USB Devices' at $189.99, which a handheld owner could plausibly want. All three are out of stock, and three products is not a merchant.

REGISTRY HAD THE PLATFORM WRONG AGAIN. It said shopify; the capture reached this shop through the Woo Store API. Corrected to woocommerce in the same commit. This is the second time the registry and a capture have disagreed on platform, and the first time cost Custom Gaming Chair a publish that shipped zero products while reading as live. The capture knew both times.
TWO REAL BUGS FELL OUT OF THIS FEED AND ARE FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT. Neither is about POWOXI and both would have bitten a merchant we do want.

BUG 1: the classifier filed a solar charge regulator as a gamepad. battlestation's `\bcontrollers?\b` matched 'with MPPT Controller' and 'Solar Charge Controller 12V 8A', and battlestation is tested before power, so three products crossed rooms. Same family as `\bamp\b` matching the unit of current. The pattern is now guarded by what precedes it; 'Xbox Controller' still lands.

BUG 2: HTML entities survived into product titles. Eleven of these titles read '... Trickle Maintainer – with MPPT Controller', and a title is escaped again on its way to the card, so the entity would have rendered as its own characters in the product name. Descriptions were already cleaned; titles never had been. Worse, the two DOM scrapers deleted `&#nnnn;` outright, which silently edits a merchant's product name and looks like whitespace tidying in a diff. There is one decoder now and row() runs it before the classifier or the card sees a title.
10 of 32 are out of stock, which is a third of the catalogue and worth knowing if this is ever revisited.
One short of the sitemap's 33. Immaterial given the recommendation.
